title: Keep file versions and observation dates separate when reading a CSV
summary:
By The Sideline

A data file can have a release date that differs from the date of its observations. A download time is a third timestamp. Treating them as interchangeable can make a dashboard appear fresher than its inputs.

The Sideline's public five-row CSV sample provides a small example. It has sample_version and value_as_of fields, plus value_type to identify the modeled quantity. In the sample checked on November 2, 2026, the version is 2026-10-11 and the value-as-of date is 2026-10-05. Those are sample dates, not a claim that the file describes today's complete athlete dataset.

title: Evaluate Vercel Flags from another project without sharing SDK keys.
summary:
Project Connections let applications evaluate flags defined in another Vercel project within the same team, without managing SDK keys.

Previously, sharing flags between projects required copying a server SDK key into an environment variable and managing it manually. Connected projects authenticate using their deployment’s identity. For local development, vercel env pull retrieves your project’s OIDC token.

Manage access from the Connections page under your project's Flags section, or with vercel flags connections in the CLI. Connections grant read-only access across all environments. The consumer deployment determines the flag environment (production deployments evaluate production flags).

In the consumer application, create an adapter with the source project’s ID.

Access can be revoked without redeploying.

title: German Income Tax Calculation in JavaScript
summary:
German Income Tax Calculation in JavaScript

German income tax is famously complicated, and for good reason: it is not a simple set of brackets. Germany uses a progressive formula with a tax-free allowance, two curved progression zones, and then flat marginal rates. If you build payroll or salary tools for the German market, a bracket lookup table will give you wrong answers. You need the actual formula.

Try the numbers yourself with the free Salary Calculator Germany on freekalc.com — enter a gross salary and see the estimated net pay after tax and social contributions.

How the German system is structured

For a single filer in 2026, the structure looks like this:

  • Basic allowance (Grundfreibetrag): income up to €12,096 is tax-free
  • Progression zone 1: €12,097
